easycoderunner.pauseAfterRun.description: Keep the external console open after success or failure. Windows waits for a key; other systems wait for Enter.

easycoderunner.runKey.markdownDescription: Keyboard shortcut for Run Active File. Choose a preset to apply it immediately. Choose **custom** to open VS Code’s Keyboard Shortcuts editor and record another key. You can also run **Easy Code Runner: Change Keyboard Shortcut** from the Command Palette. A shortcut can override another editor command. If you previously set an Easy Code Runner user binding, remove it in Keyboard Shortcuts to use these presets.

easycoderunner.executors.markdownDescription: Advanced structured executor overrides. Prefer Programming Language and Run Config in the Executors section for editing commands. Used when that language has no Run Config override. Each value has executable, args, and optional compile.

easycoderunner.programmingLanguage.description: Language whose Run Config you want to edit. Selecting a language loads its saved command below. This selection edits configuration; execution still follows the active file language.

easycoderunner.runConfig.markdownDescription: Command for the selected Programming Language. Changes save separately for each language. Example: `g++ {filename} -o {binary} && {binary}`. Use `&&` to compile then run. `{filename}` is the full source path and is quoted automatically. Other placeholders: `{directory}`, `{stem}`, `{binary}`, `{jar}`, `{css}`, `{yaml}`. Clear the field to restore the built-in runner. Use double quotes around an executable path containing spaces. Overrides here take priority over advanced Executors.

easycoderunner.windows.terminal.description: External terminal application to use on windows. The chosen application must be installed.

easycoderunner.windows.customPath.description: Executable path or command name when Terminal is set to custom.

easycoderunner.windows.customArgs.markdownDescription: Arguments for the custom terminal. Include `{script}` (generated script path) or `{command}` (command to execute). `{cwd}` is the source directory. Windows also supports `{encodedScript}` for PowerShell. Example on Unix: `["-e", "/bin/sh", "{script}"]`. Example for a Windows Terminal compatible app: `["powershell.exe", "-NoProfile", "-EncodedCommand", "{encodedScript}"]`. Each array item is one argument; do not add shell quotes around placeholders.
